reason: The text portrays Israel (בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל, 'the children of Israel') as a unified people and nation with organized military structure. Key evidence: (1) repeated use of הָעָם ('the people') as a collective body; (2) description of מַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל ('the camp of Israel'), indicating military organization; (3) political/military confrontation with Egypt as a rival nation-state with military forces (600 chariots); (4) Israel portrayed with collective agency—they flee, organize militarily, and respond to leadership. While the religious dimension is present (they cry out to Yahweh, believe in Yahweh), the primary framing is national and political: this is a narrative of a nation's exodus and military conflict, not of a religious sect or family following a deity.
